english.title: Gross indecency between men in public place
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a man, committed an act of gross indecency with another man, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), in public, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13 of and Schedule 2 to the Sexual Offences Act 1956.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a man
committed gross indecency
with another man
in a public

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
THIS OFFENCE IS NOW OBSOLETE

(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where one of the parties is under 16 years of age.
(ii) See also offence wording:H1864 for being party to/procuring the offence.
(iii) See offence wordings H2311 and H2313 for aggravated offence where the offender is over 21 years of age and the victim is a boy under 16 years.
(iv) See offence wordings H2310, H2312, H2314 and H2317 for offence where the offender is aged 16 to 20 and the victim is under 16 years.
(v) This offence is included in Schedule 1 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997. Therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the requirements of Section 2 of that Act, except the defendant need not register where his is under 20years of age or the other party is over 18 years of age.
(vi) As amended by the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 2000.
(vii) Repealed by s.140 of and Schedule 7 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003

other.penalty:

INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.
